definitions.explanation: Organic matter that has been decomposed and recycled as fertilizer for plants. Made from kitchen scraps, yard waste, and other organic materials.

examples.japanese: {生|なま}ゴミを{使|つか}って{堆肥|たいひ}を{作|つく}っている。
examples.english: I'm making compost using food scraps.

examples.japanese: {堆肥|たいひ}を{畑|はたけ}にまいて{土|つち}を{豊|ゆた}かにする。
examples.english: I spread compost on the field to enrich the soil.

examples.japanese: {家庭|かてい}で{堆肥|たいひ}を{作|つく}るためのコンポスターを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a composter to make compost at home.

notes:
RELATED TERMS:
・コンポスト: compost (loanword, sometimes used interchangeably)
・{腐葉土|ふようど}: leaf mold
・{有機|ゆうき}{肥料|ひりょう}: organic fertilizer
・{化学|かがく}{肥料|ひりょう}: chemical fertilizer

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{堆肥|たいひ}を{作|つく}る (to make compost)
・{堆肥|たいひ}をまく (to spread compost)
・{堆肥|たいひ}{置|お}き{場|ば} (compost pile/area)

COMPOST INGREDIENTS IN JAPANESE:
・{生|なま}ゴミ/{台所|だいどころ}くず (food scraps)
・{落|お}ち{葉|ば} (fallen leaves)
・{刈|か}り{草|くさ} (grass clippings)
・{枯|か}れ{枝|えだ} (dead branches)

CULTURAL NOTE:
With Japan's emphasis on waste reduction and recycling, home composting ({家庭|かてい}{堆肥化|たいひか}) has become more popular. Many municipalities encourage composting to reduce burnable waste.
